subject: Cross-border latency ops: SLO clarification and data path constraints
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-border latency ops: SLO clarification and data path constraints

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarification asks so we can size the perf validation and routing plan accurately:

1) Latency targets (p95):
   - You mentioned sub-200ms in demo notes — can you confirm target p95 for US and EU? Is APAC allowed a relaxed target?

2) Throughput & concurrency:
   - Approx steady-state RPS and expected peak concurrency (active sessions) — are we planning for bursty peaks?

3) Streaming requirements:
   - Are responses streamed token-by-token (low-latency streaming) or batched responses acceptable? If streaming, avg. message length / tokens?

4) Traffic split & residency:
   - Expected traffic split across regions (US/EU/APAC) and any strict data residency constraints (e.g., EU customer content must never leave EU).

5) Network path & egress:
   - Any dedicated VPC/VPN endpoints or cloud provider peering we should plan for? We can coordinate a short connectivity test during validation.

I've attached a one-sheet (finexa_perf_requirements.xlsx) — please fill the highlighted cells so our SRE team can generate a perf plan.

Next steps I propose after your answers:
- Redwood to propose a 2-hour perf validation window (synthetic traffic + a small sample of production-like requests)
- We build a routing policy that pins EU traffic to EU hosts and sets fallback rules for capacity events
- Share SOC2 + data-retention evidence for procurement (if needed)

If it's easier, we can set a quick 20-min sync tomorrow to walk the sheet.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
<aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Attachments: finexa_perf_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border latency ops: SLO clarification and data path constraints

Aisha / Laura —

Quick internal note on the ask and what I’d recommend we propose back to Finexa:

- Latency: target p95 = 200ms for US/EU is realistic for gen-1 traffic if sequence lengths are moderate (~256 tokens). APAC will likely be ~1.5x higher unless we deploy a regional instance there.
- Concurrency & throughput: ask them to give peak concurrent sessions rather than RPS — streaming sessions consume persistent connections and KV cache per session. For planning, model 150 active streaming sessions = safe start.
- Streaming: Redwood supports token streaming; the biggest cost is keepalive + KV cache scale. If they stream long-form (multi-k tokens) we should recommend batching at the edge for tail calls and enable prefix cache.
- Residency: we can pin model serving to EU-only hosts and ensure logs for EU sessions are stored in a EU bucket with KMS keys scoped to the region. Procurement will want a write-up of the data path.

Operational asks to include in the reply:
1) Exact traffic split percentages by region (US/EU/APAC)
2) Typical prompt + response token distribution (avg/95th)
3) Any regulated customer subsets that require on-prem or private deployment

Once we have the sheet back, I can draft a perf validation runbook with latency SLs, synthetic workload, and monitoring hooks. If they want a shorter pilot, propose a 1-week pilot with daily burst windows.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexa.com>

Cc: network_ops@finexa.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Cross-border latency ops: SLO clarification and data path constraints

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the follow-up. I filled the spreadsheet and attached our network diagram (finexa_network_diagram.pdf). Answers inline:

1) Latency (p95):
   - US: 180ms p95
   - EU: 200ms p95 (EU must be served from EU)
   - APAC: 350ms p95 (we accept higher tail there)

2) Throughput / concurrency:
   - Steady-state ~120 RPS globally, peak bursts up to 900 RPS for short windows.
   - Active streaming sessions estimate: 220 concurrent sessions at peak (mostly US-heavy).

3) Streaming details:
   - We use token-level streaming for live assistant flows. Typical responses are 150-400 tokens; occasional long-form up to ~2k tokens.

4) Traffic split & residency:
   - Expected split: US 65%, EU 30%, APAC 5%.
   - EU customer data must remain within EU boundaries (processing + logs), and any backups containing EU PII should be encrypted with EU KMS.

5) Network connectivity:
   - We can provide a temporary peering connection for the perf window. Our network team (network_ops@finexa.com) will coordinate.

We aim to run a perf validation the week of July 5 — can Redwood propose windows and a verification checklist? Procurement will also need SOC2 Type II and an explanation of data paths + retention for EU session logs.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Finexa

Attachments: finexa_network_diagram.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border latency ops: SLO clarification and data path constraints

Thanks Samir — that's exactly what we needed. Action items and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Perf validation windows: propose two 2-hour windows on July 6 at 09:00-11:00 PT and July 7 at 15:00-17:00 PT (pick one). We'll run synthetic token-streaming workload + a short sample of production-like requests.
2) Routing plan: we'll pin EU sessions to EU-only hosts and configure fallback to US-standby with redaction rules (only if EU capacity is exhausted and if you approve).
3) Data path doc: Ben will prepare a 1-pager detailing KMS scope, EU bucket configuration, and log retention policy for procurement.
4) Network test: please have your network team share peering details and a contact; we'll coordinate a small connectivity smoke test 48 hours before the window.

Ben / Laura — I marked the perf runbook as high priority. Ben, can you draft the runbook + checklist by EOD Wed so we can share with Finexa and procurement?

Samir — once you confirm which window you'd like and share the peering contact, I'll lock things in and send a calendar invite with the runbook attached.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
